description: Sabotages for win-volume-sys. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: A lock that succeeds is not tried, so FSCTL_LOCK_VOLUME and FSCTL_UNLOCK_VOLUME swapped for one another are not caught: a successful lock would hold a real volume against its users, and needs an administrator. The tests show only that each control reaches the device with no buffer and returns its own error. A volume on more than one disk is not available on a development machine, so the answer that needs a second call is had from a stand-in device (extents_via), not from a real one. The device-control helper's pending path is run through its seam, overlapped_call, with an overlapped ReadFile on a named pipe, because no file-system control pends on demand; the one call that makes it a control, the DeviceIoControl argument list, is pinned by the controls themselves, and FSCTL_REQUEST_OPLOCK, which takes input and pends until another handle writes, reaches DeviceIoControl through the pending path as well. The OVERLAPPED the control is made with is a declared blind spot (see its survives entry): a control made without one answers the same on every handle tried, FSCTL_REQUEST_OPLOCK included. The abort when the wait for a pending call fails is not reachable: the event is the helper's own. The failure of CreateEventW is not reachable either. The dependency query has never answered with an entry on a machine these tests ran on, because attaching a virtual disk needs an elevated token: its entries, their names and the reply to a buffer too small for them are tested against replies built from the structure's declared layout and a stand-in device, and whether a real entry's names lie inside the buffer the caller gave is not shown at all.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: the extents control sends a different code
sabotages.why: The function's whole meaning is the control code it sends; a neighbouring code is refused by a volume.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: the first answer may have room for no extent
sabotages.why: The device refuses a buffer with no room for one extent (measured: ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER), so a function that asks with none fails every volume.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a count of nothing in a more-data reply allocates a buffer with no room for an extent
sabotages.why: A reply that says it needs more room and counts none must not shrink the next buffer below the one extent the device requires.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: the retry is not bounded by its constant
sabotages.why: A loop that runs one more than the bound would spin on a volume whose extents keep changing and ask more often than the constant says.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a refusal by the device is retried as though it needed more room
sabotages.why: Any code but ERROR_MORE_DATA ends the attempts and is the device's own; retrying it would hide it behind a report that the extents kept changing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a call that says it wrote more than the buffer held is read
sabotages.why: A byte count beyond the buffer is the call's claim and not a fact; it is refused and not read as though the buffer held that many bytes.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a negative length is accepted as zero
sabotages.why: A length below zero is not a length; reporting it as an empty run would hide a damaged answer behind a plausible one.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: an extent's offset is read from where its length is
sabotages.why: The extents are what a flush domain is found from; reading the wrong field puts every run in the wrong place. The tests build the answer from the layout Windows fixes, not from the offsets the parser uses.
find: let start = i64_at(buffer, at + offset_of!(DISK_EXTENT, StartingOffset));
replace: let start = i64_at(buffer, at + offset_of!(DISK_EXTENT, ExtentLength));

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: an answer exactly as long as its extents is refused
sabotages.why: The usual answer is exactly the size of what it counts; a bound that is off by one refuses it.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: a negative offset is read as a very large one
sabotages.why: A device that reports a negative offset is broken, and an answer is refused rather than passed on as a run starting past the end of any disk.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: ERROR_MORE_DATA is not recognised
sabotages.why: A volume with more extents than the first answer holds, a spanned or striped one, would then fail where it should be asked again at the size it needs.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: an answer is asked for only once
sabotages.why: The second call, at the size the device reported, is what a volume on several disks needs.

sabotages.name: WV-1.2: a sector size of zero is accepted
sabotages.why: Zero is no sector size, and a geometry that says it means the answer is damaged; passed on, it would become an alignment that no power of two satisfies.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: the control is made without the OVERLAPPED it waits on
sabotages.why: A declared blind spot, measured and not assumed: on an overlapped handle a call with no OVERLAPPED is undefined, but the controls the tests reach take it without incident. That includes FSCTL_REQUEST_OPLOCK, the one control that pends: with no OVERLAPPED it blocks inside DeviceIoControl until the oplock breaks and answers the same, so no test can tell the two apart. The OVERLAPPED is there for the handle this crate is lent and cannot inspect.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: the event handed to an overlapped control does not suppress the completion packet
sabotages.why: A handle on a completion port gets a packet when an overlapped call completes unless the event's low bit is set. Without it a control would reach a consumer's loop as a completion it never asked for.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a control is told its output buffer is empty
sabotages.why: The buffer length the device is given is the buffer's own; a shorter one makes every control fail for want of room.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a control's input is not passed to the device
sabotages.why: An oplock request is refused without its input structure, so a helper that drops the input fails the control that takes one; none of the no-input controls could tell.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a control that completed reports no bytes written
sabotages.why: The byte count is what a caller checks the reply's size by; a count of nothing would read as an empty reply.
replace:
if started != FALSE {
        return Ok(written - written);

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a failure that is not pending is not returned
sabotages.why: Every failure but ERROR_IO_PENDING is the call's answer; treating the pending code as one reports a call that is still running as a failure while the device writes into a buffer about to be freed.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: the wait for a call still running does not wait
sabotages.why: The result is read without waiting, so a call that has not completed is reported as ERROR_IO_INCOMPLETE and the device is left writing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a call that completed after pending reports no bytes written
sabotages.why: The count a call that completed asynchronously wrote is read from GetOverlappedResult, and it is what a caller checks a reply's size by.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a call that failed after pending is reported as a success
sabotages.why: A call that pends and then fails reports its own code through GetOverlappedResult; discarding it would report success with whatever count was left.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a failure's code is clamped to what an i32 holds
sabotages.why: A code of 2^31 or more, such as the virtdisk errors, must reach the caller as the code it is; clamping or masking it names a different error. This is the defect win-error-codes exists to remove.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a failure is reported without its code
sabotages.why: The error is the device's own code, so a caller can read it with Win32Error::from_io; an error that carries none is not.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a buffer longer than a u32 counts is truncated and not refused
sabotages.why: A length that does not fit is refused, since passing its low bits would tell the device a different size from the buffer's own.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a buffer the machine cannot supply is reported under another code
sabotages.why: The size is the device's to name, so a buffer for it may not be allocatable; that is ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, the code a caller reads as 'ask for less'.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a reply buffer is not zeroed
sabotages.why: A reply is read only as far as the device wrote, and what it did not write must be zero and not whatever the allocation held.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a u32 is read two bytes wide
sabotages.why: A u32 is four bytes; a read two bytes wide fails to convert and every field is absent.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: control, the end of a u32 read is saturated and not checked
sabotages.why: A control: where the end would overflow, the start is past the buffer anyway and get returns None, so saturating changes the file and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: the NUMA control sends a different code
sabotages.why: Declared blind spot. Only a volume that answers tells the control code apart from a wrong one, since a wrong code and a volume with no answer are both a refusal; the machine measured answers (node 0), but a test that required it would fail on one that does not, so none does.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: the NUMA control is told its output buffer is empty
sabotages.why: The call is made with exactly the room the structure needs; with none, a device refuses for want of room whether or not it has an answer.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: a reply larger than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: A reply of any size but the structure's is refused and not read, because a value taken from a buffer the device did not fill would read as a node.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: a reply smaller than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: The other half of the size check: a short reply leaves the buffer's remainder as it was, and reading it would report a node the device never named.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: the node is read from the first byte alone
sabotages.why: The node is a whole ULONG, carried unaltered; a value above 255 would be truncated.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: a reply that is not the structure is some other kind of error
sabotages.why: A malformed reply is InvalidData, as for every other answer in this crate that does not hold what it says; a caller tells it from a device's refusal by the kind.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: control, the size check written as two comparisons
sabotages.why: A control: not-equal is less-or-greater, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the storage query sends a different control code
sabotages.why: Every storage property is this one control; a neighbouring code is refused by a disk, which the real-disk tests see.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the query names the query type where the property goes
sabotages.why: The property id and the query type are two fields of one structure; a swap asks a different question of a different property.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the query writes the property where the query type goes
sabotages.why: The other half of the same swap: the query type has its own field.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: additional parameters are not sent
sabotages.why: A property that reads them would be asked its bare question whatever the caller passed.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the input is only as long as its parameters need
sabotages.why: The device requires the whole structure whatever the parameters; a shorter input is ERROR_BAD_LENGTH.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the first buffer may be smaller than the header
sabotages.why: A buffer smaller than the header is refused by the device (ERROR_BAD_LENGTH or ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER, by property), so the loop never asks with less.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the retry runs one more time than its bound
sabotages.why: The bound is what stops a size that keeps changing from being asked for forever, and it is used exactly.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a call that says it wrote more than the buffer held is read
sabotages.why: A byte count beyond the buffer is the call's claim and not a fact; it is refused and not read as though the buffer held that many bytes.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a reply that exactly fills the buffer is refused
sabotages.why: The edge of the check above: a reply the size of its buffer is the usual shape of a reply that fits.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a reply shorter than its header is read
sabotages.why: Fewer bytes than the header cannot say how big the reply is; what is in the rest of the buffer is not the device's.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a reply that says it is smaller than its own header is returned
sabotages.why: A size below the header's own is not a size; truncating to it would return bytes that cannot be the reply.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a reply whose size is what was written is asked for again
sabotages.why: The usual answer is exactly the size it names; a bound off by one turns every reply into a malformed one.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a reply shorter than the size it names, in a buffer of exactly that size, is asked for again
sabotages.why: Asking again at a size the buffer already had gets the same buffer and the same answer.
find:
if size <= buffer.len() {
                    return Err(invalid_data("a reply shorter than the size it names"));
replace:
if size < buffer.len() {
                    return Err(invalid_data("a reply shorter than the size it names"));

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a header-only reply is asked for again at a different size than it names
sabotages.why: The size the header names is the size to ask for; any other is a buffer that is not the reply's.
find:
// The header alone, or less than the reply: ask again at the size it names.
                capacity = size;
replace:
// The header alone, or less than the reply: ask again at the size it names.
                capacity = size + 1;

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: ERROR_MORE_DATA is not asked for again
sabotages.why: The disk answers a buffer between the header and the reply with ERROR_MORE_DATA and the header written; not recognising it fails every reply larger than the first buffer.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a more-data reply is asked for again at a different size than it names
sabotages.why: As for the header-only reply: the size the header names is the size to ask for.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a more-data reply that names a size already given, in a buffer of exactly that size, is asked for again
sabotages.why: The edge of the check that stops a device that keeps saying so from being asked at the same size forever.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the reply's size is read from its version
sabotages.why: The header is a version then a size; reading the first for the second makes every reply one byte long.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: control, the buffer check written the other way round
sabotages.why: A control: a > b is b < a, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the first buffer is the header and no more
sabotages.why: A smaller first buffer returns the same bytes at the cost of a second call; what is pinned is that the reply measured, 112 bytes, still costs one.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a query for existence is made as a standard query
sabotages.why: An existence query returns no structure, so read as one it is a reply shorter than its header.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the generic query swaps the property and the query type
sabotages.why: The two newtypes exist so they cannot be swapped by a caller; a swap inside would make them mean nothing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the exists query type is the mask query's value
sabotages.why: The named query types are the values Windows defines.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the unique id asks for a different property
sabotages.why: The property is the function's whole meaning; another property's reply does not hold the sections this reads.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the device descriptor is read from the id descriptor's offset
sabotages.why: Each section has its own offset field; a neighbour's reports one section twice.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: an offset of zero is a section
sabotages.why: Zero is where the header is, so it is how a section that is not there is said.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a section that starts right after the header is refused
sabotages.why: The first section starts exactly at the end of the header, which is where the device puts it.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a section may be smaller than its own header by one byte
sabotages.why: A section's own size covers its own header, so one smaller is not a size.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a section that ends exactly at the end of the reply is refused
sabotages.why: The last section ends where the reply does; a bound off by one refuses the usual answer.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: a section's size is read from the start of the section
sabotages.why: A section is a version then a size; reading the first for the second delimits it wrongly.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the identifier's size is read from the wrong field
sabotages.why: The layout is the device's; the real disk's header says how long its reply is, and the field it is read from is checked against that.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the disk NUMA function asks for a different property
sabotages.why: Another property's reply is larger than the NUMA descriptor, and reads without error as three numbers; the size the descriptor says it has is what tells them apart.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the node is read from the size's field
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: WV-2.4: the NUMA version is read from the node's field
sabotages.why: As for the node: each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the version is not put in the buffer
sabotages.why: The version is an input: the call refuses a buffer whose version field is not 1 or 2, so a function that does not set it is refused on every machine.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a first size below the structure is not raised
sabotages.why: A buffer under the structure's own size is ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, so asking at a configured smaller size would fail where raising it succeeds.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a size no larger than the one given is asked for again
sabotages.why: A reply that needs more room and names the room it already had is not going to be answered by asking the same question again.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the buffer is regrown to a size other than the one named
sabotages.why: The size the call names is the size it was measured to need; asking for a different one is a guess.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: ERROR_MORE_DATA is not a reason to ask again
sabotages.why: Which of the two a buffer too small for the entries returns is unverified, so both are followed.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: only one attempt is made
sabotages.why: A reply that needs more room than the first buffer has is only answered by asking again.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a status is altered on its way out
sabotages.why: The code is carried as the call returned it; the virtdisk errors have values above 16 bits, and one truncated to 16 bits names a different error.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the real call is given a size of nothing
sabotages.why: The size is how much the call may write; the real calls are the only test of the argument list.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the real call is not given the flags
sabotages.why: The flags are which way the query looks; without them the host direction is never asked for.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: HOST_VOLUMES also sets the disk-handle bit
sabotages.why: Each flag is its own bit; a flag that also says the handle is a disk asks a different question.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a reply that used more than it was given is read
sabotages.why: The call says how many bytes it used; a number beyond the buffer is a reply that cannot be trusted, and slicing by it would read outside the buffer.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a version one reply is read with version two's entry size
sabotages.why: The entries of each version have their own size, and the second entry of a reply is found by it.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a count the reply cannot hold is accepted up front
sabotages.why: The count is checked against the bytes the call used before any entry is read, so the refusal names the count and not whichever entry was reached first.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the ancestor level is read from the provider flags
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the type flags are read from the provider flags
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the device id is read from the vendor field
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the vendor is read from one byte late
sabotages.why: The vendor GUID is the sixteen bytes at its own offset.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: the host volume is read from the dependent volume's pointer
sabotages.why: Each name is read from the pointer the structure has for it, and the four are distinct.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a version one reply is read for names
sabotages.why: Names exist only in version two; reading them from a version one entry reads the next entry's bytes as pointers.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a null name pointer is not none
sabotages.why: A null pointer is an absent name, not an address to refuse.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a name pointer at the end of the reply is taken as inside it
sabotages.why: A pointer at the first byte past the reply is outside it, and is refused for that and not for what reading there would find.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a name with no room for its terminator is accepted
sabotages.why: A string that runs to the end of the bytes used has no terminator within them, and what follows is not the call's.
replace: let terminated = offset + units.len() * size_of::<u16>() <= reply.len();

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: a name ending exactly at the end of the reply is refused
sabotages.why: The boundary the previous entry is one past: a terminator in the last two bytes used is within them.

sabotages.name: WV-2.5: control, the two statuses that ask again written the other way round
sabotages.why: A control: an or-pattern's alternatives are unordered, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WV-3.1: the device number control sends a different code
sabotages.why: The function's whole meaning is the control code it sends; the geometry control answers a volume with a structure whose first fields are not a device number.

sabotages.name: WV-3.1: the device number is read from the partition number's place
sabotages.why: The number and the partition are told apart only by their place in the structure; a volume's disk and its partition differ.

sabotages.name: WV-3.1: a reply too short for the structure is read as zeros
sabotages.why: A reply that does not hold the structure must be refused; zeros would be taken for a device number.
find: .ok_or_else(|| invalid_data("a reply shorter than a device number"))
replace:
.or(Some(0))
                .ok_or_else(|| invalid_data("a reply shorter than a device number"))

sabotages.name: WV-3.1: control, the reply buffer sized by its constant and not its type
sabotages.why: A control: the structure is three u32s, twelve bytes, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
